p: The ad opens with dynamic text asking who reviews an agent-written spec over a dimmed document. It transitions to an inline document review interface where a user leaves feedback to cut timeline from 6 weeks to 3 weeks. It then switches to a terminal running a CLI command using Claude to apply review comments, shows the updated document live on the same URL with resolved comments, and closes on a clean call-to-action screen.
Artifact Share lets teams review and comment on AI-generated docs at a single URL, allowing AI agents to automatically apply revisions and update the live document.

[{"timestamp":"00:00","observation":"Kinetic text hook introduces the core workflow question over a blurred UI background."},{"timestamp":"00:06","observation":"Zoomed view shows text selection and comment submission smoothly."},{"timestamp":"00:11","observation":"Terminal prompt executes agent doc edits via CLI."},{"timestamp":"00:20","observation":"Document updates with comment status resolved in the side panel."},{"timestamp":"00:23","observation":"Clean final end card displays core value prop and URL."}]

The video executes the narrative arc clearly with purposeful pacing and focused zooms. Typography remains legible at mobile feed scale, and the terminal sequence effectively conveys the AI integration. Pacing during the terminal output feels slightly long, but overall presentation is cohesive.

p: The comment -> CLI edit -> republished v2 sequence clearly demonstrates the core mechanic (humans point, agents edit, same URL) and the Artifact Share badge stays visible in every frame, so product salience and clarity are strong. But the hook is a dense, static doc screenshot rather than anything kinetic, undercutting the 'kinetic hook' intent and risking a scroll-past on X. The final CTA button ('Try it free -> artifactshare.com') renders with washed-out, low-contrast white text on a light gray pill, which weakens click intent and reads as a minor render defect rather than a confident close.
